design.read: From now on, repairs no longer reach you one by one by email and text. Everyone sends a request through one form, and every request lands as a row in one list. You see who it is from, where it is, what it is about, how urgent it is and when it is needed, all in the same place, so you can book someone to come without piecing details together.

material.label: Your repair form
items:
Who is this from?
Their own words

Where is the problem?
Their own words

What is the problem?
Their own words

How urgent is it?
Emergency, water or safety risk
Urgent, needs to be fixed in a day or two
Normal, can wait for the next visit

When do you need someone to come?
Their own words

material.label: Your message with the link
items: Hi all, to report a repair, please use this form instead of emailing or texting me: [link]. It takes a minute. Tell me who you are, where the problem is, what is wrong, how urgent it is and when someone can come. If there is water or a safety risk, please also call me right away. Thanks, [your name]

material.label: Your repair list columns
items: When do you need someone to come?

steps.say: Create the form. Tally has written the questions for you.
Send the form answers to a sheet, so every request becomes a row in one list.
In the Status column, add a drop down with these choices: New, Booked, Done. Put the same kind of drop down in Who is booked if you like.
Color the emergency rows so they stand out. Tally has written the formula for you.
Share the form link with tenants and colleagues, using the message Tally wrote.
Each time, open your list, read the new rows, book someone for each one, and set the Status to Booked. Send people back to the form if they text or email you a repair.

design.good: Every repair arrives as one row with all five details filled in, and you book someone without having to ask follow up questions.
design.approval: Check each emergency row yourself and confirm the details and the day before you book anyone to come.

answers.text: Bldg 2, Unit 3B, bathroom: slow drain and small drip under sink. Needs plumber, booked for Thursday. Hallway light out by the stairs, handyman to replace bulb and check fixture.

design.read: From now on, your inspection notes go straight from your phone into rows for your sheet. You keep jotting notes the way you do today, then paste them in with your saved instructions and get clean rows back. You stop retyping each note by hand across your 40 apartments.

material.label: Your inspection instructions
items: I will paste in my inspection notes. Turn them into rows for my sheet, one row per issue found. Use exactly these columns, in this order: Date, Building, Unit, Place, What was found, What needs doing. Date: write the date of the inspection as [date], or leave it blank if I did not give one. Building: for example Bldg 2. Unit: for example 3B. Place: the room or area, for example bathroom or hallway. What was found: the problem in a few plain words. What needs doing: the action and who does it, and the day if I gave one. If one note has two problems, make two rows. Never add details I did not give. Show the rows as a table I can copy into Google Sheets.

If a line does not fit the columns, do not drop it. Put it in a last row with the full line copied word for word in What was found, and write [check] in What needs doing. Leave any column you cannot fill blank, and never guess.

steps.say: Open a new Google Sheet and type the six column names in the first row, in this order.
Save your inspection instructions in ChatGPT so you can use them again each month.
Paste your phone notes under your saved instructions and let ChatGPT turn them into rows.
Read each row against your notes, then copy the rows into the next empty rows of your sheet.

design.tryOn: This month's notes from one building.
design.good: Every issue in your notes is one row in your sheet, with the right unit, place and action, and nothing added that you did not write.
design.approval: Check every row against your own notes, especially unit numbers, dates and who is booked to do the work, and look at any row marked [check].

prep.aboutNote: I am a property manager for 40 rental apartments in three buildings. I handle repairs, tenant requests, move ins and move outs, and inspections. I often paste in my own rough notes from my phone and want them turned into clean, short rows for a Google Sheet. I like plain, direct wording with no extra chat. Never add details I did not give, such as dates, names, prices or causes. If something is unclear, leave it blank or mark it with [check] and ask me. Never drop a line of my notes. Keep tenant names and private details out of your answers.
safeUse: Never type tenant names, phone numbers or email addresses into ChatGPT.
Leave out door codes, keys, lockbox details and passwords.
Do not paste lease terms, rent amounts or payment details.
Use unit numbers and plain descriptions of the problem only.
Read every row before it goes into your sheet.
